adjudication_rationale: Interrupted IPC JIT builds could leave stale locks and hang diffusion warmup; cold-cache multi-rank warmup coverage matches the failure. Sides with coder B.
A Triton kernel branch involving a None pointer needed constexpr handling, and a sink_ptr=None kernel test would reproduce the crash. Sides with coder B.
Mamba cache block tables and CUDA-graph buffers were sized without speculative slots, causing prefix-cache-all/spec-decode crashes. Sides with neither coder.
Deterministic RNG made concurrent FlashInfer MNNVL jobs reuse socket opIds, colliding collective state under concurrent schedules. Sides with coder A.
The Mamba2 SSD varlen kernel used the wrong boundary offset for larger chunk/block cases, which edge reference tests catch. Sides with coder B.
The SGLang RMSNorm replacement changed HF rounding order; strict kernel-vs-HF reference tests can catch it, while MMLU shows impact. Sides with coder B.
The PR fixes stale CUDA-graph token counts, padded-row MoE routing, and input-embedding replay state that can corrupt batched outputs. Sides with coder B.
Fused MoE applied dequantization, bias, routed weights, and casts in the wrong order for quantized bias cases; reference tests can expose it. Sides with coder B.
The AMD HIP layernorm wrapper used the wrong fused_add_rms_norm signature, causing AMD CI/runtime failures. Sides with neither coder.
NPU MTP unquant settings for a draft model incorrectly affected the main model, so full NPU serving with mixed quantization is primary. Sides with coder B.
Long EAGLE/speculative positions could exceed the RoPE cache and trigger illegal memory access; long-position edge tests are the cheapest detector. Sides with neither coder.
The ROCm quantized MoE loader crashed on a 0-D scale tensor, a ROCm model-load matrix plus scale-shape tests issue. Sides with coder A.
FlashInfer read FusedMoE layers from a mixed forward context and asserted they were Attention layers under a DP MoE launch. Sides with coder B.
The FlashInfer sampler NaN-detection path crashed after an API/signature change; a sampler test with nan detection enabled is direct. Sides with neither coder.
The no-shared-stream MoE path used hidden states after in-place mutation, corrupting ROCm model output in full serving. Sides with coder A.
The draft-extend CUDA-graph metadata used the wrong stride for topk>1 and bs>1, producing NaNs. Sides with coder B.
NaN candidate logits were dropped by the selector and led to duplicate block IDs and sparse-slot assertions; NaN/sparse-logit distributions are key. Sides with coder B.
The FlashInfer MoE routing dtype bug changed Mistral Large 3 from empty output to a correct response, requiring model-level inference coverage. Sides with coder A.
The PR fixes a silent performance fallback to cuBLAS and explicitly reports no numerical issue or severe availability failure. Sides with coder B.
DeepSeek-R1 FP4 TP8 speculative serving hung or failed until prior MoE/quantization commits were reverted; full B200-class serving coverage is plausible. Sides with coder A.
The record says old Triton MoE configs were copied to fix a CI regression but does not show a concrete correctness symptom. Sides with coder B.
The ROCm/AITER DeepSeek torch-compile test failed in the MoE/fp8 path, making a ROCm compile lane the primary missing coverage. Sides with coder A.
The TRTLLM ragged DeepSeek prefill path expected a workspace buffer absent on CutlassMLAImpl and crashed at serving time. Sides with neither coder.
The ModelOpt/TRTLLM FP4 MoE path used local rather than global expert counts, which configuration tests over TP/EP expert layouts can trigger. Sides with neither coder.
RoutingMethodType selection broke one-group Renormalize MoE models such as Mistral Large 3, best caught by model-level serving plus config tests. Sides with neither coder.
The Triton GDN conv1d kernel mixed fp16 activations and bf16 state across branches, a dtype/compiler edge not tied to one GPU. Sides with neither coder.
The allreduce/RMS fusion had a tensor-parallel-size-one edge bug; a TP=1 configuration test is the direct detector. Sides with coder A.
The record establishes a tuning-script/config-function crash, not production kernel behavior in serving. Sides with coder B.
The ROCm AITer backend rejected valid grouped-query head layouts; unit coverage over GQA shapes on ROCm would catch the over-broad guard. Sides with coder B.
The CUDA-only post_residual_addition fix missed non-GPU backends, implying backend-specific numerical behavior best caught by a hardware/backend matrix. Sides with coder B.
